Rashi on Berakhot 43a:10:1.hebrew: מכלל דאיכא עדיף מיניה - ואפ"ה, כיון דאתחיל בחדא, עביד לאידך:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:10:1.english: By implication, there is [someone] greater than him - And even so, since he began with one [blessing], he performs the other.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:1.hebrew: הנוטל ידיו תחלה - במים אחרונים, הוא מזומן לבהמ"ז:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:1.english: One who washes his hands first - With the final water, he is designated for Grace after Meals.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:2.english: He saw him - Rabbi Ḥiyya [saw] Rav.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:3.hebrew: דהוה מרתת - שמא ראה ידי מלוכלכות, או שמא הארכתי באכילה יותר מדאי:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:3.english: That he was trembling - [Fearing:] "Perhaps he saw that my hands were dirty, or perhaps I lingered over eating too much."

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:4.hebrew: עיין בברכת מזונא קאמר לך - כאן נתן לך רשות לברך בהמ"ז, שהנוטל ידיו תחלה הוא מברך:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:12:4.english: He is telling you to review Grace after Meals - Here he granted you permission to recite Grace after Meals, for one who washes his hands first recites the blessing.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:13:2.english: Its column - The plume of smoke that rises straight up and ascends.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:13:3.hebrew: הא לא ארח - לא הריח בו עדיין ולא נהנה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:13:3.english: But he has not smelled - He has not yet smelled it and has not derived benefit.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:14:1.hebrew: מברכין עליהן בורא עצי בשמים - ואע"פ שנשרף ואינו בעין, אלא שהתימור עולה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:14:1.english: One recites over them "Who creates fragrant trees" - And even though it is burned and is not present in substance, but rather the column [of smoke] rises.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:14:2.english: Except for musk - Mosga, in Old French.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:14:3.english: Which is from an animal - From the excrement of an animal.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:15:1.english: They raise an objection: One only recites "Who creates fragrant trees" over balsam - For the wood itself comes before us.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:15:2.english: Of the house of Rabbi and of the house of Caesar - [The baraita] mentioned these because it is found only in the house of kings and people of greatness.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:15:3.hebrew: ועל ההדס שבכל מקום - וה"ה לכל הדומה להם, שהעץ עצמו מריח בלא שרפה, אלא דהדס שכיח, ודברו חכמים בהווה בכל מקום. ומוגמר לא מברכינן אלא בורא מיני בשמים:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:15:3.english: And over myrtle everywhere - And the same applies to anything similar to them, where the wood itself is fragrant without burning; rather, myrtle is common, and the Sages spoke of the prevalent [case] everywhere. And over incense, we recite only: "Who creates various kinds of spices."

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:17:1.english: Balsam oil, what blessing does one recite - [When reciting a blessing] over its fragrance.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:17:2.hebrew: שמן ארצנו - שהיה גדל ביריחו, ועל שם הריח היתה נקראת יריחו. והוא פנג האמור בספר יחזקאל (כ"ז): ״יהודה וא"י המה רוכליך בחיטי מנית ופנג״ — כך ראיתי בספר יוסף בן גוריון:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:17:2.english: The oil of our land - For it used to grow in Jericho, and on account of the fragrance [re'ach], it was called Jericho [Yericho]. And it is the pannag mentioned in the Book of Ezekiel (27): "Judah and the Land of Israel were your merchants, with wheat of Minnith and pannag" — so I saw in the book of Yosef ben Gurion.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:17:3.english: Except for Rav Yehuda - Do not bring me proof from his words in this [matter].

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:19:2.hebrew: משחא כבישא - שמן שבו טמון הקושט, והשמן מריח מן הבושם שבתוכו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:19:2.english: Steeped oil - Oil in which the costus is immersed, and the oil smells of the spice that is inside it.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:19:3.english: Ground oil - That they ground costus into it.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:19:4.hebrew: לא - הואיל ואין נראה לעינינו אלא השמן:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:19:4.english: No - Since only the oil is visible to our eyes.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:1:1.hebrew: אהדר קרעיה לאחוריה - קרע שקרע בהספד רבו — החזיר החלוק לאחוריו ומה שלאחור לפנים, כדי לקרוע קרע אחר, להראות אבל עכשיו כיום המיתה, על שהיו צריכים להוראה ואין יודעים להורות:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:1:1.english: He turned his tear behind him - [As for the] tear that he had rent at the eulogy of his teacher — he turned the tunic behind him and that which was behind to the front, in order to rend another tear, to display mourning now as on the day of [his] death, over [the fact] that they needed a ruling and did not know how to rule.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:1:2.hebrew: רמי להו כו' - כדרמינן לעיל. וע"כ מבעי ליה לאוקומי ברייתא בהכי, וקתני: ״אחד מברך לכולם״ — דקביעות הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:1:2.english: He raised a contradiction to them, etc. - As we raised [a contradiction] above. And perforce, one must establish the baraita in this [manner], and it teaches: 'One recites a blessing on behalf of all of them' — for it is [a formal] establishment [of a meal].

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:1.english: They brought them water - Such was their custom.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:2.english: Washes one of his hands - To receive with it the cup that he drinks before the meal.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:3.english: They went up - Onto the couches and reclined.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:4.english: He washes both of his hands again - For he needs to eat with both of them.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:5.hebrew: אע"פ שכל אחד ואחד ברך לעצמו - צריכין עוד ברכה, שאין ברכה ראשונה פוטרתו; שאין הראשון קרוי שלפני המזון, שאינו במקום סעודה, והאי בתרא הוא יין שלפני המזון:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:5.english: Even though each and every one recited a blessing for himself - They need another blessing, for the first blessing does not exempt it, as the first [wine] is not called "before the meal," since it was not in the place of the meal; and this latter [wine] is the wine before the meal.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:6.hebrew: אחד מברך לכולן - דכיון דהסבו, הוקבעו:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:4:6.english: One recites a blessing for all of them - For since they reclined, they have become established [as a group].

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:5:1.english: The first clause is difficult - For it teaches: 'Each and every one recites a blessing for himself.'

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:6:1.hebrew: שאני אורחין דדעתייהו למיעקר - סופן למיעקר ולעלות ולהסב במקום אחר, שאין זה מקום המסיבה, אלא כאן ישבו עד שיתכנסו כל הקרואים. ודרך בעלי בתים עשירים היה לזמן לסעודתם אורחים עניים, להכי קרי להו אורחים. והא דאמר רב יין לא בעי הסבה, אלא ישיבה בעלמא — שלא בשעת סעודה קאמר, או בשעת סעודה ובמקום סעודה:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:6:1.english: Guests are different, as their intention is to uproot [themselves] - They will ultimately uproot [themselves] and go up and recline in another place, for this is not the place of reclining; rather, here they sat until all the invited guests would assemble. And it was the practice of wealthy householders to invite poor guests to their meal; therefore, [the baraita] calls them "guests." And that which Rav said, that wine does not require reclining, but rather mere sitting [suffices] — he was speaking of when it is not at the time of a meal, or at the time of a meal and in the place of the meal.

Rashi on Berakhot 43a:9:1.hebrew: הואיל ואין בית הבליעה פנוי - ואין לב המסובין אל המברך, אלא לבלוע:
Rashi on Berakhot 43a:9:1.english: Since the throat is not empty - And the attention of the diners is not on the one reciting the blessing, but rather on swallowing.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:14:1.english: Over all the incense one recites: "Who creates fragrant trees" - [This applies] even though they have been burned and the fragrant trees are not physically present.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:15:1.hebrew: ועל ההדס שבכל מקום - בעל הלכות גדולות לא גריס תיובתא, ומשני: "תנא הדס וכל דדמי ליה" — כלומר: שעיקרו לריח, לאפוקי תפוחים וחבושים שאין עיקרן לריח אלא לאכול. ומי שהולך בבית שיש שם בשמים, ויש שם מיני בשמים שמריח בהן, ומספקא ליה אי ממין עץ אי ממין אדמה הוא — יש מפרשים שמברך "שהכל נהיה בדברו", דעל כולן אם ברך "שהכל" יצא; והרב רבינו משה מקוצי היה אומר שיברך "בורא מיני בשמים":
Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:15:1.english: "And over myrtle everywhere" - The Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot does not read 'a conclusive refutation' [teyuvta], and [the Gemara] answers: The tanna taught [the case of] myrtle and anything similar to it — meaning, [plants] whose primary purpose is for fragrance, to exclude apples and quinces, whose primary purpose is not for fragrance, but to be eaten. And one who walks into a house where there are spices, and there are various kinds of spices that he smells, and he is in doubt whether it is from a species of tree or from a species of the earth — some explain that he should recite: "...by Whose word all things came to be" [Shehakol nihyeh bidvaro], for regarding all of them, if one recited Shehakol, he has fulfilled his obligation; and the master, Rabbeinu Moshe of Coucy, would say that he should recite: "Who creates various kinds of spices" [Borei minei besamim].

Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:19:1.hebrew: משחא כבישא - פי' ר"ח: שמענו מרבותינו שכובשין שומשמין, וורד ועצי בשמים זמן מרובה, וקולטין השומשמין ריח של בשמים, וסוחטים וטוחנים אותם, ויש בו ריח של בשמים. ומשחא טחינא — קרוב לטחינתו נותנים עליהם עצי בשמים, ואינו קולט כל כך הריח:
Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:19:1.english: "Steeped oil" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: We have heard from our teachers that they steep sesame seeds, roses, and fragrant wood for an extended period, and the sesame seeds absorb the scent of the spices, and [then] they press and grind them, and it has the scent of spices in it. And [as for] ground oil — close to its grinding, they place fragrant wood upon them [the sesame seeds], and it does not absorb the scent as much.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:4:1.hebrew: כל אחד נוטל ידו אחת - מפני כבוד הברכה. ולא דמי לנוטל ידיו לפירות, דהוי מגסי הרוח — כיון שאינו נוטל שתי ידיו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:4:1.english: "Each one washes one hand" - [This is] out of respect for the blessing. And it is not comparable to one who washes his hands for fruit, who is [considered] among the haughty of spirit, since he does not wash both of his hands.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:4:2.hebrew: בא להם יין וכו' - אע"ג דיין שלפני המזון פוטר יין שלאחר המזון, כ"ש זה שלפניו הוא — שאני הכא: כיון שעלו להסב, הוי שנוי מקום וצריך לברך:
Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:4:2.english: "Wine came before them, etc." - Even though wine [drunk] before the meal exempts wine [drunk] after the meal, [and] all the more so this [wine], which is [also] before it [the meal] — it is different here: since they went up to recline, it constitutes a change of place, and one must recite a blessing.

Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:9:1.hebrew: הואיל ואין בית הבליעה פנוי - וי"מ: כשאומר "סברי מורי", והם מניחין לאכול כדי לשמוע הברכה ולענות אמן — שיהיו פטורים. וכן משמע בירושלמי גבי הך ברייתא: ה"מ באורחין, אבל בבעל הבית — פטור, מפני שהכל פונים אצל בעל הבית; תני רבי חייא: אף בעל הבית בתוך ביתו. ואין נראה לרבינו אלחנן, דכיון שתקנו חכמים שיברך כל אחד לעצמו — אינו יוצא כלל בברכת חבירו; וגם שלא תחלוק בין פנוי לשאינו פנוי, דאתי למטעי. והטוב והמטיב — יש מפרש שפוטר לאחרים לכולי עלמא, דהכי משמע: "הטוב" — לעצמו, "והמטיב" — לאחריני, שהם שותים ממנו. ורבינו יחיאל היה אומר: דלא היא, דשייך נמי "אין בית הבליעה פנוי", ולא פליג בין הטוב ובין ברכת היין; דמשום האי טעמא, "הטוב" לדידיה ו"מטיב" לאחריני — אינו פוטר אחרים, דהא "המטיב" שייך אפי' שלא בפני המטיבין לו, כדאמרי' לקמן בפרק הרואה (ברכות דף נט:): אמרו לו "ילדה אשתך זכר", אומר: "ברוך הטוב והמטיב" — "הטוב" לדידיה, "והמטיב" לאשתו, אע"ג דאין אשתו אצלו. אבל צריך עיון קצת מהבדלה, שאנו מבדילין ועומדים: היאך אנו פוטרין זה את זה מיין ומהבדלה, אחרי שאין אנו לא יושבים ולא מסובין? ושמא י"ל: מתוך שקובעין עצמן כדי לצאת ידי הבדלה, קבעי נמי אכולה מילתא; ולכך נאה וטוב למבדיל וגם לשומעים שישבו בשעת הבדלה, שאז יהיה נראה כקבע, ופוטר אותם:
Tosafot on Berakhot 43a:9:1.english: "Since the throat is not free" - And some explain that when [the one reciting the blessing] says, "Pay attention, my masters" [savrei morai], and they pause eating in order to hear the blessing and answer "Amen," they are discharged. And so it implies in the Yerushalmi regarding this Baraita: These matters [that each recites the blessing for himself] apply to guests; but in the case of the host, [they are] discharged, because everyone turns [their attention] to the host. Rabbi Chiyya taught: Even a host in his own home [does not discharge them]. And it does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Elchanan, for since the Sages instituted that each and every one should recite the blessing for himself, one does not fulfill [his obligation] at all through another's blessing; and also so that you do not distinguish between [a throat that is] free and one that is not free, lest [people] come to err. And regarding [the blessing of] HaTov VeHaMeitiv: There is [an authority] who explains that [one person] discharges others according to all, for this is what it implies: "Who is good" — to himself, "and does good" — to others, who drink from it. And Rabbeinu Yechiel would say that this is not so, for [the rationale that] "the throat is not free" applies [here] as well, and [the halakhah] does not distinguish between [the blessing of] HaTov and the blessing over wine. For on account of that reason — ["Who is good" for himself and "does good" for others] — he does not discharge others, since "and does good" applies even not in the presence of those to whom good is done, as we say below in chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 59b): If they said to him, "Your wife gave birth to a male [child]," he says: "Blessed... Who is good and does good" — "Who is good" to himself, and "does good" to his wife, even though his wife is not with him. However, [our custom] requires some consideration regarding Havdalah, where we recite Havdalah while standing: How do we discharge one another from [the blessing over] the wine and from Havdalah, since we are neither sitting nor reclining? And perhaps one can say: Since they establish themselves [together] in order to fulfill the obligation of Havdalah, they establish [themselves] regarding the entire matter as well. And therefore, it is fitting and good for the one reciting Havdalah and also for the listeners to sit at the time of Havdalah, for then it will appear as an established gathering, and he [validly] discharges them.
